title: Nonreciprocity reversal of magnetoacoustic attenuation in NiFe alloy thin films
authors: Mingran Xu, Kei Yamamoto, Kouta Kondou, Zheng Zhu, Liyang Liao, Kiyohiro Adachi, Tomoka Kikitsu, Daisuke Hashizume, Dirk Grundler, Sadamichi Maekawa, Yoshichika Otani
abstract: Nonreciprocity, the asymmetry of transport, underlies technologies from the diode to the microwave isolator. In a ferromagnet, a surface acoustic wave generates an elliptical effective field with propagation-locked handedness, breaking the reciprocity of its propagation. Despite decades of study on this phenomenon, a method for controlling the sign of the nonreciprocity has remained elusive. Here we observe a sign reversal in Ni$_x$Fe$_{100-x}$ films. A 0.8 at.% change across Permalloy's zero-magnetostriction composition, where the magnetoelastic coefficient $b$ changes sign, reverses the handedness of the elliptical effective field and thereby the nonreciprocity, from 78.6% to -61.8%. Angle-dependent measurements and spin-wave-ellipticity modelling show that reversing the sign of $b$ reverses the handedness of the elliptically polarized effective field. Aided by cubic frequency scaling, we resolve the sign of $b$ down to -0.05 MPa in a 10-nm film, establishing nonreciprocity as a nanoscale probe of magnetoelastic coupling.
summary: This work demonstrates that nonreciprocity in magnetoacoustically coupled thin films can be used as a highly sensitive, nanoscale diagnostic tool. By observing the sign reversal of this asymmetry across different alloy compositions, the authors successfully linked the phenomenon to the underlying change in the magnetoelastic coupling coefficient $b$. This establishes a new method for characterizing fundamental magnetic material properties.
main_problem: The study aims to understand and control the sign of nonreciprocity arising from magnetoacoustic attenuation in ferromagnet thin films.
main_result: A small compositional change near Permalloy's zero-magnetostriction point causes a measurable sign reversal of the nonreciprocity, confirming that this effect can serve as a nanoscale probe for the magnetoelastic coupling coefficient $b$.
method: The research uses Surface Acoustic Waves (SAWs) propagating through $	ext{Ni}_x	ext{Fe}_{100-x}$ thin films deposited on a piezoelectric substrate to measure nonreciprocal attenuation ratios ($\chi_P$).
model_or_system: The physical system is a hybrid device structure involving an $	ext{LiNbO}_3$ substrate, Interdigital Transducers (IDTs), and the magnetic trilayer. The underlying physics involves magnetoacoustic coupling between SAWs and the ferromagnet's magnetization.
key_observables: Nonreciprocity ratio ($\chi_P$), which measures the asymmetry of SAW attenuation for counter-propagating waves; the sign and magnitude of the magnetoelastic coefficient ($b$).
important_parameters: Compositional concentration $x$ (near 80 at.% Ni), magnetic field angle $\phi$, and SAW frequency ($f \approx 2-9 	ext{ GHz}$).
main_assumptions: The nonreciprocity is attributed to a rotation-based mechanism (MR or Barnett) rather than the shear-strain mechanism, which fails to explain the observed sign reversal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device setup and show clear evidence of nonreciprocity reversal ($\chi_P$) as the composition $x$ crosses the point where the magnetoelastic coefficient $b$ changes sign. Frequency dependence analysis is also presented.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical mechanism by analyzing how compositional tuning controls the sign of $\chi_P$. It then uses theoretical modeling (comparing shear-strain vs. rotation mechanisms) to pinpoint the origin, culminating in demonstrating that nonreciprocity acts as a sensitive probe for $b$ near zero.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism and acoustics, the ability to use an electrical/acoustic measurement ($\chi_P$) to precisely determine the sign of a fundamental material parameter ($b$) where direct strain measurements fail is analogous to using quantum signatures (like entanglement measures) to probe inaccessible aspects of many-body Hamiltonians.
